title: It won't die
briefing: A wedged process ignores your polite requests to stop.
tips: `kill -9 PID` sends SIGKILL, which a process cannot catch or ignore.
objective: Force-kill the stuck-daemon process that ignores a normal kill.
hints: A plain kill sends a signal the process can ignore — and this one does.
`kill -9` (SIGKILL) cannot be ignored. You'll need its PID.

reactions.say: Still running — it ignored SIGTERM. Send the one signal it can't refuse: kill -9.

explanation: A normal kill sends SIGTERM, which programs may catch to clean up — or ignore. `kill -9` sends SIGKILL, which the kernel enforces with no chance to refuse. Use it only when the polite signal fails.
